claims.text: A high density of chemically complex, coherent interfaces between HEA layers impedes dislocation nucleation.
A high density of chemically complex, coherent interfaces between HEA layers impedes dislocation motion.
Coherent interfaces between HEA layers impede atomic diffusion.
The interfacial impediment of dislocations and diffusion increases the effective activation energy for creep.
Slight compositional or microstructural variations between chemically similar HEA layers can create a high density of coherent interfaces.
Diffusion- and dislocation-mediated plasticity are active under the proposed high-temperature, moderate-to-high-stress conditions.
Layer thicknesses from tens of nanometers to a few hundred nanometers are small enough for interfacial effects to be significant.
Interfaces between the alternating layers induce lattice distortions.
Interfaces between the alternating layers induce compositional gradients.
The layer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation glide and climb.
Alternating HEA layers possess intrinsic lattice mismatch and chemical disorder that disrupt continuous dislocation motion and atomic rearrangement.
The layered interfacial structure increases the creep stress exponent relative to a homogeneous HEA microstructure.
Multilayer HEA coatings will have lower steady-state creep strain rates than composition- and thickness-matched monolithic HEA coatings.
Multilayer HEA coatings will have higher creep stress exponents than composition- and thickness-matched monolithic HEA coatings.
Multilayer HEA coatings will have longer creep lifetimes than composition- and thickness-matched monolithic HEA coatings.
The proposed mechanism is applicable where diffusion- and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms dominate.
The interfacial strengthening effect diminishes when layer thickness greatly exceeds the interaction length scale for dislocation motion.
The interfacial strengthening effect diminishes when the interfaces are insufficiently coherent.
